scope: Defensive catalog of publicly documented living-off-the-land execution primitives. Probes are inert; no payloads, no persistence, no network.
taxonomy: group and method name the defensive family; platform separates Windows from Linux/Unix.

techniques.name: Mshta
techniques.abuse: Runs HTML applications and embedded VBScript or JScript, including content referenced by URL, UNC path or script: moniker.
techniques.probe: Inventory only; optional inert marker probe.
techniques.detection: mshta with http, https, UNC, file, script: or vbscript: arguments. mshta spawning powershell, wscript, cscript, cmd or rundll32. Network connections from mshta.
hardening: Block mshta with WDAC or AppLocker if it is not required.
Enable ASR rule Block executable content from email and webmail.

tree.a: User opens an HTA attachment or a link to one
Signed binary parses remote HTA and runs the script inside itself
HTA starts a shell to stage the next step
Download or beacon over HTTPS

cmd.w: mshta should not accept remote content or a script: moniker in normal use.

asr.n: Block executable content from email client and webmail
Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content

net.w: Any outbound 80/443 from mshta.exe is abnormal. Alert on first connection and keep the destination.

fix: Block mshta.exe with AppLocker or WDAC unless a line-of-business app needs it.
Enable the two ASR rules in block mode.
Turn on 4688 command-line auditing and Sysmon 1 so the parent chain is visible.
Remove the .hta association for standard users.

techniques.name: Windows Script Host - VBScript
techniques.abuse: Runs .vbs, .vbe and .wsf files through the Windows Script Host, including remote or user-writable paths.
techniques.detection: wscript started from temp, downloads or user-writable paths. wscript spawning powershell, cmd, mshta or rundll32. Script arguments containing URLs.
hardening: If VBScript is not needed, block wscript and cscript with WDAC or AppLocker.
Set the Windows Script Host Enabled policy to 0 on managed hosts that do not require it.

tree.a: User opens a script attachment or archive member
Windows Script Host runs VBScript from disk or a share
Script shells out to run built-in tools
Fetch the next stage

cmd.w: Normal logon scripts run from a fixed path. Script hosts launching shells or download tools are the pattern to catch.

asr.n: Block executable content from email client and webmail
Block all Office applications from creating child processes

net.w: Warn on any wscript.exe egress; it has no legitimate reason to reach the internet on a workstation.

fix: Set WSH Enabled=0 by policy if no logon script needs it.
Block wscript.exe through AppLocker script rules.
Enable 4688 cmdline and AMSI so the script body is visible.
Alert on wscript.exe children outside the logon-script window.

techniques.name: Windows Script Host - JScript
techniques.abuse: Runs .js and .jse files through the console script host.
techniques.detection: cscript with //E:jscript, remote paths or temp paths. cscript spawning powershell, cmd or mshta.
hardening: Block cscript with WDAC or AppLocker if JavaScript is not required.
Prefer allow-listing over blocking individual extensions.

tree.a: Script lands in a temp or user-writable path
Console script host runs JScript
Script runs whoami, ipconfig, net view
Script performs the download itself

cmd.w: cscript in a user path, especially with //E, is a scripting-host execution signal.

asr.n: Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content
Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts

net.w: cscript.exe opening a socket is rare in managed environments; alert and capture the destination and bytes out.

fix: Disable WSH by policy where scripts are not required.
Block script extensions in AppLocker Executable and Script rules.
Enable PowerShell and AMSI telemetry to capture script content.
Alert on cscript.exe with a non-system script path.

techniques.name: Rundll32
techniques.abuse: Calls exported DLL functions and can reach script engines through url.dll or mshtml, including javascript: and vbscript: arguments.
techniques.detection: rundll32 with javascript:, vbscript:, shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL or ordinal exports. DLLs loaded from temp or downloads. rundll32 with no arguments from an Office process.
hardening: Block rundll32 only where it is not needed by installed software.
Use WDAC to restrict DLLs that may be loaded by signed system binaries.

tree.a: Dropper or macro writes a DLL or scriptlet
Runs an export, an ordinal or a remote scriptlet
DLL runs code in the host and spawns a shell
Beacon from a process that should not have a network role

cmd.w: Ordinal-only exports, javascript: prefixes and DLLs from user-writable paths are the classic rundll32 abuse shapes.

asr.n: Block all Office applications from creating child processes
Block Office applications from injecting code into other processes
Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: Track rundll32.exe egress and DLL loads from user paths. The combination is the indicator.

fix: Enable ASR Office child-process and code-injection rules.
Alert on rundll32 with ordinal exports or user-path DLLs.
Use WDAC to allow only signed DLLs from system paths.
Keep Sysmon 7 (image load) enabled to catch the DLL.

techniques.name: Regsvr32
techniques.abuse: Squiblydoo: /s /n /u /i:URL scrobj.dll loads a remote scriptlet through the COM scriptlet engine.
techniques.detection: regsvr32 with scrobj.dll, /i:http, /i:https or /i:\\ paths. Network connections from regsvr32. regsvr32 spawning script hosts.
hardening: Enable ASR rule Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands where applicable.
Restrict outbound HTTP from system binaries with egress filtering.

tree.a: User is pointed at a remote scriptlet
Registers a remote COM scriptlet (squiblydoo)
Scriptlet runs JScript inside regsvr32
Second stage fetched in the same process

cmd.w: regsvr32 with /i: pointing at a URL or scrobj.dll is the documented squiblydoo pattern.

asr.n: Block executable content from email client and webmail
Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: Alert on regsvr32.exe egress, especially to a host that also served the .sct reference.

fix: Block regsvr32.exe for standard users via AppLocker.
Enable ASR block on untrusted executables.
Log 4688 with cmdline and alert on /i: with a URL.
Restrict outbound traffic from system binaries that never need it.

techniques.name: Msiexec
techniques.abuse: Installs packages from remote URLs, runs DLLs with /y and applies transforms that can execute code.
techniques.detection: msiexec /i with http or UNC paths. msiexec with /q /n and no visible installer. msiexec spawning rundll32, cmd or powershell.
hardening: Disable installation of packages from untrusted locations with AppLocker or WDAC.
Enable installer logging and centralize MSI operational events.

tree.a: User is sent an MSI link or attachment
Installs a remote or user-path MSI quietly
Custom action runs a command
Package or payload fetched from the internet

cmd.w: Quiet MSI installs from a URL or a user-writable path are the abuse shape.

asr.n: Block executable content from email client and webmail
Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: Watch msiexec.exe fetching an MSI over HTTP(S) and any child process it starts.

fix: Require signed MSI packages through AppLocker or WDAC.
Alert on msiexec with a URL argument or a user-path package.
Log 4688 cmdline and MSI installer events.
Disable MSI installs for standard users where possible.

techniques.name: InstallUtil
techniques.abuse: Runs .NET assemblies through the InstallUtil helper, including code in Install and Uninstall methods.
techniques.detection: installutil with /logfile=, /LogToConsole=false or /U. installutil loading assemblies from temp or downloads.
hardening: Block installutil with WDAC or AppLocker if development tooling is not needed on the host.
Restrict .NET assembly execution paths.

tree.a: Compiled assembly is dropped
Runs managed code through the installer utility
Assembly executes in the signed host
Managed payload beacons

cmd.w: InstallUtil with suppressed logging and a user-path assembly is the documented abuse flag set.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria
Block all Office applications from creating child processes

net.w: Any egress from installutil.exe is abnormal outside a maintenance window.

fix: Remove InstallUtil use where .NET installers are not needed.
Alert on /logfile= with /LogToConsole=false.
Enable Sysmon 7 and .NET runtime logging.
AppLocker allow-list for developer binaries.

techniques.name: MSBuild
techniques.abuse: Executes inline tasks defined in a project file.
techniques.detection: MSBuild building projects from temp, downloads or user-writable paths. MSBuild spawning csc, powershell or cmd.
hardening: Remove MSBuild from general-purpose hosts where it is not needed.
Block project files from untrusted locations with WDAC.

tree.a: Project file with an inline task lands on disk
MSBuild compiles and runs inline C#
Inline task spawns a command
Build host beacons

cmd.w: MSBuild on a project in a user-writable path, outside a build agent, is the signal.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria
Block all Office applications from creating child processes

net.w: Egress from msbuild.exe on a workstation is abnormal; alert with the project path.

fix: Allow MSBuild only on build hosts, block elsewhere with AppLocker.
Alert on project files under user profiles.
Enable 4688 cmdline and .NET runtime logging.
Keep Sysmon 1 and 11 for the project file and child chain.

techniques.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
techniques.abuse: Creates processes locally or remotely, and can load XSL transforms.
techniques.detection: wmic process call create, /node: remote targets, format:http or format:\\ paths. WMI-created children of wmiprvse.exe.
hardening: Restrict remote WMI with firewall rules and least privilege.
Monitor WMI activity with Sysmon 19, 20 and 21.

tree.a: Loader writes an XSL or command
WMI spawns a process or formats a remote XSL
Same command aimed at a peer over DCOM/RPC
Command registers a permanent consumer

cmd.w: wmic process call create and remote /node: use are the high-value patterns; wmic is deprecated but still present.

asr.n: Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands
Block persistence through WMI event subscription

net.w: Watch RPC 135 and dynamic RPC ports from wmic.exe toward peers; this is the lateral-movement leg.

fix: Enable ASR block for PSExec and WMI process creation.
Alert on permanent WMI consumers.
Restrict RPC between workstations at the network layer.
Remove wmic.exe where the environment does not need it.

techniques.name: Cmstp
techniques.abuse: Installs connection manager profiles from INF files and can execute commands from the profile.
techniques.detection: cmstp with /s, /ni or an INF file from temp. cmstp spawning cmd, powershell or rundll32.
hardening: Block cmstp with WDAC or AppLocker if VPN profiles are not deployed through it.
Restrict INF execution from user-writable paths.

tree.a: INF file with a malicious service section lands on disk
Installs a connection profile and runs the command in it
INF RunPreSetupCommands executes
Staged command downloads

cmd.w: cmstp with /s and an INF from a user path is the known bypass shape.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: Egress from cmstp.exe or its immediate child is abnormal on a workstation.

fix: Block cmstp.exe unless VPN profiles are provisioned centrally.
Alert on /s or /ni with a user-path INF.
Enable 4688 parent tracking.
Prefer centrally deployed VPN profiles.

techniques.name: Odbcconf
techniques.abuse: Registers DLLs with /A {REGSVR} and can execute exported code.
techniques.detection: odbcconf with /A {REGSVR} or DLL paths from temp. odbcconf spawning rundll32.
hardening: Block odbcconf if ODBC setup is not performed on the host.
Restrict DLL load paths with WDAC.

tree.a: Response file lands on disk
Runs REGSVR through a response file
Unsigned DLL loaded into the signed host
DLL beacons

cmd.w: odbcconf with /a or /f and REGSVR is the documented proxy-execution pattern.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: odbcconf.exe has no reason to reach the internet; alert on any egress.

fix: Remove odbcconf.exe where ODBC setup is not required.
Alert on /a and /f arguments.
Allow only signed DLLs through WDAC.
Track DLL loads with Sysmon 7.

techniques.name: MMC
techniques.abuse: Loads Microsoft Management Console files and COM snap-ins.
techniques.detection: mmc loading an .msc file from temp or downloads. mmc spawning script hosts or cmd.
hardening: Block unsigned .msc files with WDAC or AppLocker.
Restrict MMC snap-in execution to administrative accounts.

tree.a: Console file with an embedded snap-in or script
Loads a user-supplied console file
Snap-in or embedded script runs code
Snap-in performs network activity

cmd.w: A .msc outside the system management folder is the indicator.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: Egress from mmc.exe is not normal; correlate with the console file path.

fix: Restrict .msc execution to administrators.
Alert on console files in user-writable paths.
Enable 4688 cmdline.
Allow-list MMC snap-ins through AppLocker.

techniques.name: Xwizard
techniques.abuse: Instantiates COM classes by CLSID and can proxy execution.
techniques.detection: xwizard with a CLSID argument, especially followed by child processes.
hardening: Block xwizard with WDAC or AppLocker if it is not used.
Restrict COM class activation.

tree.a: DLL plus a registration entry
Runs a registered wizard class from a DLL
Wizard class executes in the signed host
Wizard code beacons

cmd.w: xwizard RunWizard with a class GUID is the proxy-execution signature.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: Any xwizard.exe egress is abnormal.

fix: Block xwizard.exe for standard users.
Alert on RunWizard and GUID arguments.
Monitor registry class registration (Sysmon 12/13).
WDAC allow-list for signed DLLs.

techniques.name: Forfiles
techniques.abuse: Runs an arbitrary command through /c for each matching file.
techniques.detection: forfiles /c with powershell, cmd, wscript or mshta. forfiles used from a script host parent.
hardening: Block forfiles if it is not required.
Enable command line auditing so the /c argument is visible.

tree.a: A wrapper script is written
Indirect command execution through /c
The /c payload runs
Download the next stage

cmd.w: forfiles with /c is a known indirect-execution wrapper; normal use is rare.

asr.n: Block all Office applications from creating child processes

net.w: Egress from forfiles.exe or its child on a workstation is suspicious.

fix: Alert on forfiles with /c.
Block forfiles.exe through AppLocker where unused.
Enable parent-child process logging.
Segment egress so system binaries cannot reach the internet directly.

techniques.name: Pcalua
techniques.abuse: Runs a program through the Program Compatibility Assistant with -a.
techniques.detection: pcalua -a with powershell, cmd or a binary from temp.
hardening: Block pcalua with WDAC or AppLocker if it is not used.
Audit parent/child chains from pcalua.

tree.a: Program Compatibility Assistant target lands on disk
Runs an arbitrary binary via -a
The target executes
Payload beacons

cmd.w: pcalua -a pointing at a user-path executable is the documented pattern.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: Egress from pcalua.exe children is abnormal; keep the parent link.

fix: Alert on pcalua with -a.
Block pcalua.exe where compatibility troubleshooting is not needed.
Log 4688 child process with parent.
Apply WDAC to user-writable paths.

techniques.name: Certutil
techniques.abuse: Downloads files with -urlcache and decodes base64 content with -decode.
techniques.detection: certutil -urlcache -split -f, -decode, -encode or -verifyctl with remote URLs. Files written to temp or startup paths.
hardening: Block certutil with WDAC or AppLocker if certificate tooling is not needed.
Apply egress filtering and alert on system binaries making HTTP requests.

tree.a: Operator or script composes the certutil line
Downloads a file with -urlcache -split -f
Decodes a base64 blob with -decode
HTTP(S) transfer from a certificate utility

cmd.w: certutil should not download URLs or decode arbitrary blobs in normal certificate operations. This is the highest-value single match in the catalog.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: Primary network control: alert on certutil.exe opening 80/443 to any host that is not a known certificate or update endpoint, then capture bytes out. Correlate with the -urlcache cmdline.

fix: Alert on certutil with -urlcache, -split, -decode or a URL.
Watch certutil.exe egress and block it at the firewall outside update windows.
Restrict outbound 80/443 to a proxy that logs the user agent and URL.
Enable 4688 cmdline and Sysmon 3/22 to join the process to the flow.

techniques.name: BITS Jobs
techniques.abuse: Transfers files and can attach a notify command line that runs after the transfer.
techniques.detection: bitsadmin /transfer, /addfile, /SetNotifyCmdLine or jobs that outlive their parent. BITS transfers from system binaries.
hardening: Monitor the BITS client operational log.
Restrict BITS jobs to approved applications with WDAC or AppLocker.

tree.a: Operator builds a BITS job
Creates and starts a transfer job
Sets a command to run when the job completes
Transfer runs inside the BITS service, not bitsadmin.exe

cmd.w: BITS jobs can survive reboot and run a notify command. The command line is the reliable detection point because the transfer itself runs in svchost.exe.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: BITS transfers appear as svchost.exe egress, so process-name egress rules alone will miss them. Join BITS-Client job events (job created, URL) to the svchost flow, or block BITS to unknown hosts at the proxy.

fix: Alert on bitsadmin /transfer and /SetNotifyCmdLine.
Enable the BITS-Client operational log and forward it.
Proxy BITS traffic so destinations are visible.
Remove completed and queued jobs you did not create; never delete jobs blindly.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.abuse: Runs encoded, hidden or downloaded commands and can load assemblies in memory.
techniques.detection: powershell -enc, -nop, -w hidden, IEX, DownloadString, FromBase64String or AMSI bypass strings. PowerShell children of Office, browsers or script hosts.
hardening: Enable script block logging and transcription.
Enable ASR rules for script and Office child processes.
Use Constrained Language Mode and WDAC for high-risk users.

tree.a: Macro or HTA composes a PowerShell line
Runs a hidden, encoded or download-and-execute command
Download cradle or module fetch
Attempt to weaken a protection (should be blocked, not just logged)

cmd.w: The detector that matters is content (4104/AMSI), not just the command line. Alert on hidden plus encoded plus a download verb in the same block.

asr.n: Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts
Block all Office applications from creating child processes

net.w: Track powershell.exe egress by destination and frequency; baseline admin tooling so a new destination stands out.

fix: Enable script block logging (4104) and AMSI output.
Enable the ASR obfuscated-script rule in block mode.
Constrain Language Mode or use WDAC for PowerShell.
Alert on hidden plus encoded arguments from an Office parent.

techniques.name: Compiled HTML Help
techniques.abuse: Opens CHM files, which can launch embedded content.
techniques.detection: hh.exe opening .chm files from temp, downloads or email attachments. hh.exe spawning cmd or powershell.
hardening: Block CHM files from untrusted zones with Attachment Manager.
Block hh.exe with WDAC or AppLocker if help files are not used.

tree.a: Compiled help file arrives
Opens a CHM that runs embedded HTML/script
CHM topic launches a command
Remote content fetched

cmd.w: A CHM from a user-writable path, especially with a child process, is the abuse shape.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: hh.exe egress is abnormal on a workstation.

fix: Remove the .chm association for standard users.
Alert on hh.exe with a user-path CHM.
Block child processes from hh.exe via ASR if available.
Log 4688 parent-child chains.

techniques.name: Regasm and Regsvcs
techniques.abuse: Registers .NET assemblies and can run code during registration.
techniques.detection: regasm or regsvcs with assemblies from temp or downloads. Child processes after registration.
hardening: Remove .NET SDK tooling from general-purpose hosts.
Block registration utilities with WDAC.

tree.a: Managed DLL dropped
Registers and runs managed code
DLL runs in the signed host
Managed payload beacons

cmd.w: RegAsm or RegSvcs on a user-path DLL is the pattern; both are developer tools that should not run on endpoints.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: Egress from regasm.exe is abnormal outside a deployment window.

fix: Remove .NET SDK tooling from endpoints.
Alert on user-path DLL registration.
Enable Sysmon 7 for the image load.
WDAC allow-list for signed assemblies.

techniques.name: Control Panel
techniques.abuse: Loads .cpl applets, including files from user-writable paths.
techniques.detection: control.exe loading a .cpl file from temp or downloads. control.exe spawning cmd or powershell.
hardening: Block unsigned .cpl files with WDAC or AppLocker.
Restrict Control Panel applets to approved paths.

tree.a: Control panel applet or DLL dropped
Launches a user-supplied applet
Applet code runs in the signed host
Applet beacons

cmd.w: control.exe with a file path is not normal use; applets are normally opened by name.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: control.exe egress is abnormal.

fix: Alert on control.exe with a path argument.
Block .cpl from user-writable paths.
Enable Sysmon 7 for DLL loads.
AppLocker allow-list.

techniques.name: Mavinject
techniques.abuse: Injects a DLL into a running process with /INJECTRUNNING.
techniques.detection: mavinject /INJECTRUNNING. This binary is rare on workstations and is high signal when it appears.
hardening: Block mavinject with WDAC or AppLocker on general-purpose hosts.
Monitor Sysmon 8 for remote thread creation into sensitive processes.

tree.a: DLL dropped and target chosen
Injects a DLL into a running process
Remote thread runs the DLL
Injected code uses the host process network identity

cmd.w: mavinject is an App-V component; injection arguments on an endpoint are a strong signal.

asr.n: Block Office applications from injecting code into other processes
Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: Correlate egress from the injected host process, not from mavinject. Keep Sysmon 8/10 for the injection event.

fix: Block mavinject.exe where App-V is not deployed.
Enable ASR code-injection rules.
Keep Sysmon 8 and 10 and forward them.
Restrict SeDebugPrivilege to administrators.

techniques.name: Windows Command Shell
techniques.abuse: Chains commands, expands variables and launches other interpreters.
techniques.detection: cmd /c with encoded or heavily concatenated commands. cmd spawning script hosts or network utilities in sequence.
hardening: Enable command line auditing.
Alert on unusual parent/child chains rather than blocking cmd outright.

tree.a: Parent composes a command chain
Runs a chained download and execute
whoami, ipconfig, net, tasklist
Download via a system binary

cmd.w: Track cmd.exe where the parent is an Office process or where the child is a download tool.

asr.n: Block all Office applications from creating child processes

net.w: Watch the child process egress, not cmd.exe itself; cmd is the wrapper.

fix: Enable ASR Office child-process blocking.
Alert on Office to cmd.exe.
Keep 4688 with cmdline so the full chain is in one event.
Segment egress through a logging proxy.

techniques.name: Verclsid
techniques.abuse: Verifies COM class identifiers and can proxy execution.
techniques.detection: verclsid /S /C {CLSID}, especially when followed by child processes.
hardening: Block verclsid with WDAC or AppLocker if it is not required.
Restrict COM class activation.

tree.a: COM server DLL dropped
Verifies a COM class and loads its server
COM server runs in the signed host
COM server beacons

cmd.w: verclsid with /S /C and a class GUID is the known proxy-execution pattern.

asr.n: Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age or trusted list criteria

net.w: verclsid.exe egress is abnormal.

fix: Alert on verclsid with /S /C.
Block verclsid.exe for standard users.
Monitor COM class registration.
WDAC allow-list for signed DLLs.
